label: Church
_model: Interior kernel. A parish church wants to be believed, attended, given to, or kept holy, and its accommodations are what a cure of souls does to keep a flock.

appeasement.move: say the words of the creed aloud, as though you meant them
appeasement.why: it is believed by someone living

appetites.want: never to preach to an empty nave
appetites.purpose: the pews would never be empty

appeasement.move: take a seat in a pew and stay for the whole of it

appetites.want: to be tithed to the last sheaf
appetites.asks: "What did you put in the plate?"

appeasement.move: put something in the plate, and let it be seen

appetites.purpose: nothing unclean would ever come in

appeasement.move: clean your boots and uncover your head before you enter

accommodations.text: bricked {conscript} into the wall to pray without stopping
held {conscript} to a vow they could not possibly keep
buried {conscript} under the flagstones so they would always attend
tithed {conscript} down to the last sheaf and then the seed corn
barred {conscript} from the door and would not say the words over them
would not release {conscript} from service, and then could not

relic.label: the relic that was never once doubted
relic.function: the only thing here anyone truly believed in

bell.label: the bell that called a full nave
bell.function: the only thing that ever brought them all in

chalice.label: the chalice the tithes were counted into
chalice.function: the only place the parish was ever generous

register.label: the register of who was and was not clean
register.function: the only record of who was let in

factions.name: the Congregation
factions.essence: still attending a service that has not ended

factions.name: relic-hunters
factions.essence: here for what is under the altar

factions.name: what was barred out
factions.essence: got in eventually, by another door

triggerGlossary.announced: came in by the west door, in daylight, as a congregation does
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: caught by two of the walled-in, or by a squint and a window
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice under a vault carries further than you think
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed in a pew longer than a prayer takes

foes.name: Skeleton
foes.note: fearless; will not leave its pew

skirmish.avoid: they do not rise for anyone who sits down

fight.line: 1 Ghoul in the charnel and 2 Skeletons

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: on a hit, a free Called Shot to freeze for a round

fight.avoid: the Ghoul will not cross consecrated ground — stay on the flags

battle.line: 1 Necromancer at the altar and 3 Skeletons

foes.name: Necromancer
foes.note: raises one from the floor per round

battle.harmedBy: anything — but they keep coming until he stops
battle.avoid: he will hear a confession before he fights; it costs a Turn

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith of the Vicar, 1 Ghoul and 4 Skeletons

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: it will not strike anyone kneeling

faith.dangerLine: the church can tell who believes and who is only standing here

institution: a creed cut into the chancel arch, every letter re-gilded
pews numbered and assigned, none of them free
a squint cut so the priest can see who is not attending
ritual: a candle relit at the same hour by nothing
a service book open at the same page for three centuries
holy water in a stoup that has not evaporated
demand: a rail you are expected to kneel at before you pass
a chancel step you cannot cross without being asked a question
a font that fills when you look at it
wound: a rood with the figure hacked off and the cross kept
statues with their faces smoothed by hands, not weather
a creed with one line scratched out by many people
anchor: a reliquary with the seals unbroken
a relic-box let into the altar stone
a monstrance under cloth, still warm

features: a candle lit this week in an empty church
a service book moved to a different page
fresh water in the stoup
a pew re-cushioned by somebody
a hymn number left on the board
kneelers set out in a row, recently

decisions.cue: a rail you are expected to kneel at
decisions.cost: kneeling is submission and it is also protection

resolve.success: you kneel and the Congregation counts you faithful — nothing here strikes a kneeler
resolve.failure: you pass without kneeling and are marked: the next encounter starts hostile
resolve.orElse: go round by the aisle: one Turn, and you are noticed avoiding it

decisions.cue: a creed with one line scratched out
decisions.cost: saying the missing line aloud would settle an old argument

resolve.success: you work out the scratched line and say it — the church relaxes entirely
resolve.failure: you guess wrong and say something the church considers heresy: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: say the creed without the line; it is accepted, coldly

decisions.cue: a reliquary with the seals unbroken
decisions.cost: opening it settles whether there was ever anything in it

resolve.success: you open it without breaking the seals and see what is inside
resolve.failure: you break the seals and whatever was believed in stops being believed: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it sealed; the question stays open, which suits the church

decisions.cue: a rood with the figure hacked away
decisions.cost: restoring it is a kindness; asking who did it is not

resolve.success: you set the figure right and the Congregation is grateful — they will guide you
resolve.failure: you drop it: the noise brings everything, roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it; the cross is bare and the church resents the indifference

decisions.cue: a font that fills when you look at it
decisions.cost: using it is a claim on the church's protection

resolve.success: you use it properly and are counted clean for the rest of the delve
resolve.failure: you use it carelessly and it empties: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: walk past dry; nothing gained, nothing owed

decisions.cue: a squint cut through the wall at eye height
decisions.cost: looking through sees who is being watched

resolve.success: you look and see the whole nave, including what is standing in it
resolve.failure: you are seen looking, from the other side
resolve.orElse: do not look; you go in blind

situations.doing: holding a hymn book open at a page it cannot read
situations.onArrival: it offers you the book and waits
situations.because: the service cannot continue until someone sings
situations.offer: sing anything at all and the whole nave joins, and stands aside

situations.doing: praying through a slot in a wall, without pausing
situations.onArrival: the prayer stops mid-word
situations.because: she was walled in to pray without ceasing and has
situations.offer: give her something to pray for and she will tell you what she has heard through the wall

situations.doing: levering at an altar stone with a bar
situations.onArrival: they stop and offer you the other end
situations.because: the relic is under it and they cannot shift it alone
situations.offer: help and they will split what is under it

situations.doing: lighting themselves along the nave, one at a time toward you
situations.onArrival: the nearest one takes
situations.because: the service is being prepared
situations.offer: light one yourself and the church treats you as clergy

situations.doing: standing for a hymn that has not been announced
situations.onArrival: they look at you, waiting for the number
situations.because: the hymn board is blank and nobody has set it
situations.offer: name any number and they sit, and let you through

situations.doing: digging a grave inside the church, in the aisle
situations.onArrival: it looks up and asks who it is for
situations.because: it was told to dig and not told for whom
situations.offer: give it a name — not one of yours — and it will dig elsewhere

temptations.cue: a finger-bone in a silver case
temptations.benefit: once, be believed absolutely by anything here
temptations.standingDrawback: the church knows its relic is out of the building

temptations.cue: a phial of water from the stoup
temptations.benefit: once, make ground temporarily consecrated
temptations.standingDrawback: what was already there has to go somewhere

temptations.cue: a service book, much used
temptations.benefit: once, say the right words in a rite you do not know
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected to lead the next one

temptations.cue: a splinter from the hacked rood
temptations.benefit: once, refuse a supernatural effect entirely
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever you refused finds someone else in the party

temptations.cue: a set of hymn-board numerals
temptations.benefit: once, summon the Congregation to a place you choose
temptations.standingDrawback: they stay until the hymn is finished, and nobody knows the tune

congregation.dangerLine: the church is still counting the house, and you have just walked in

institution: pews with family names carved on the ends, all of them occupied
a gallery built to hold a hundred more
ritual: a bell rung for a service nobody is walking to
a collection taken up along an empty row
banns read out for a marriage between two dead people
demand: a pew with a gap in it exactly your size
a seating plan with your place already marked
a nave arranged so a latecomer must walk the length of it
wound: pews torn out and the fixings left
a gallery collapsed under a weight it was never given
attendance rolls with the numbers falling year on year, in one hand
anchor: a bell, unhung, with the rope still on it
a full attendance roll, one Sunday, framed
a hat still on its peg, brushed

features: a pew polished by somebody this year
a hat on a peg that was empty before
an attendance roll with a fresh entry
a collection plate with coin in it
a bell-rope replaced recently
a door propped open, welcomingly

decisions.cue: a pew with a gap in it exactly your size
decisions.cost: sitting is attendance and attendance is binding

resolve.success: you sit for a moment and stand — counted present, and nothing here troubles you
resolve.failure: you sit and stay: the service continues around you and you lose a Turn
resolve.orElse: stay standing at the back; the Congregation resents it visibly

decisions.cue: a collection plate coming down an empty row
decisions.cost: the plate reaches you whether anyone carries it or not

resolve.success: you give well and are counted generous — the church opens for you
resolve.failure: you give nothing and the plate follows you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: give everything you carry loose: generous, and you are poorer

decisions.cue: a bell-rope, replaced recently, in a tower with no ringer
decisions.cost: ringing calls the parish, and something answers

resolve.success: you ring it and the Congregation assembles where you want them
resolve.failure: you ring badly and something else assembles: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave the rope; the parish stays where it is

decisions.cue: banns read for a marriage between two of the dead
decisions.cost: objecting is your right and it will be heard

resolve.success: you object on a technicality and the church is delighted by the correctness
resolve.failure: you object badly and are held to have slandered the dead: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: hold your peace; the marriage proceeds and something is now bound

decisions.cue: an attendance roll with your names already written
decisions.cost: somebody entered you before you arrived

resolve.success: you find who wrote it and why, and can use it
resolve.failure: you strike your names out and the church takes the absence badly: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; you are expected weekly from now on

decisions.cue: a gallery that will hold you or will not
decisions.cost: the stair up is the fast way over the nave

resolve.success: you cross the gallery and it holds
resolve.failure: it gives: 2 Grit each and everything in the church looks up
resolve.orElse: go round at floor level: one Turn

situations.occupant: a full nave of the Congregation
situations.doing: sitting through a service with no priest
situations.onArrival: every head turns as you enter, politely
situations.because: the service was never dismissed
situations.offer: take a seat for one minute and they will let you through the chancel

situations.doing: showing an empty pew to nobody
situations.onArrival: it turns and shows you to it instead
situations.because: every guest must be seated
situations.offer: take the seat and it will show you anything else you ask for

situations.doing: travelling along an empty row toward you
situations.onArrival: it stops in front of you
situations.because: the collection must be taken and never is
situations.offer: put anything in and the row lets you pass

situations.doing: prising a brass off a pew end
situations.onArrival: they freeze and one raises a crowbar, uncertainly
situations.because: the brasses are worth more than the box
situations.offer: let them work and they will tell you which floor-slab is loose

situations.doing: ringing itself for a service nobody is coming to
situations.onArrival: the rope moves without a hand
situations.because: the hour must be rung
situations.offer: catch the rope and ring it properly, and the Congregation gathers for you

situations.doing: keeping a place with a hat and a folded coat
situations.onArrival: it moves them aside for you
situations.because: the place is kept for someone who never came
situations.offer: sit in the kept place and it will tell you who it was for

temptations.cue: a small hand-bell from the vestry
temptations.benefit: once, gather everything in the church to one room
temptations.standingDrawback: they stay until dismissed by name

temptations.cue: a hat from the peg row, brushed
temptations.benefit: the Congregation takes you for a parishioner
temptations.standingDrawback: you are expected at the next service

temptations.cue: a collection plate, worn thin
temptations.benefit: once, ask for something and have it given
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever is given is expected back at a hundredfold

temptations.cue: a page of the attendance roll
temptations.benefit: once, prove you were present somewhere you were not
temptations.standingDrawback: your absence elsewhere is now on record

temptations.cue: a brass off a family pew
temptations.benefit: doors that check standing open for you
temptations.standingDrawback: the family it names is remembered as yours

offering.dangerLine: the church is owed a tithe, and it has kept every account

institution: a tithe barn attached to the church and bigger than it
a poor box with three locks and three keyholders
a board listing what each field owes, in bushels
ritual: a first sheaf brought in and never threshed
a plate passed along a row that nobody sits in
candles bought by subscription, each with a name
demand: a box at the door you cannot pass without hearing
a plate held out at the chancel step
a room where every surface has somewhere to put a coin
wound: a poor box forced from behind, the locks intact
a tithe board with the last three years blank
a barn emptied in a night, and the parish starved for it
anchor: a chalice the tithes were counted into
a strongbox under the altar, still locked
a tally of every sheaf ever given

features: a fresh candle bought and named
a poor box emptied and put back straight
coin left on a ledge, deliberately
a sheaf laid at the altar this season
a tithe board with a new figure
a lock changed on the poor box

decisions.cue: a poor box with three locks and no keyholders left
decisions.cost: opening it is theft or restitution depending who you ask

resolve.success: you open it as the churchwardens would and take only what is owed you
resolve.failure: you force it and the parish counts you a thief: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; the money stays where the parish put it

decisions.cue: a first sheaf laid at the altar and never threshed
decisions.cost: threshing it releases something the church has been holding

resolve.success: you thresh it properly and the church counts a debt cleared — it eases toward you
resolve.failure: you scatter it and the offering is spoiled: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it; the debt stands

decisions.cue: a plate held out at the chancel step by nothing at all
decisions.cost: what you put in is measured against what you carry

resolve.success: you give proportionately and the church is satisfied for the whole delve
resolve.failure: you give meanly and it is noticed: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: give nothing; the plate follows you at a distance

decisions.cue: a tithe board with three blank years
decisions.cost: filling them in is a lie the church might accept

resolve.success: you enter plausible figures and the arrears are considered settled
resolve.failure: your figures are impossible and the church knows every field: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the blanks; the arrears stand against the parish, not you

decisions.cue: a chalice used for counting rather than communion
decisions.cost: using it properly might be the point

resolve.success: you use it as it was meant and the church gives up what it was holding
resolve.failure: you drink from it as a cup and it is profaned: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; it goes on holding coin

decisions.cue: a candle bought by subscription with a name on it
decisions.cost: lighting someone else's candle is presumption

resolve.success: you light it and the named person's account is credited — they will help you
resolve.failure: you light it wrongly and the subscription lapses
resolve.orElse: leave it unlit; it has been unlit a long time

situations.doing: counting coin into a chalice that never fills
situations.onArrival: it asks whether you have come to pay or to be paid
situations.because: the account has never balanced
situations.offer: pay anything and it will unlock what it is guarding

situations.doing: standing fuller than the church and quite silent
situations.onArrival: the doors are open and nothing has been taken
situations.because: the tithe was gathered and never distributed
situations.offer: take a share openly and the parish counts you owed

situations.doing: carrying a sheaf toward the altar, reluctantly
situations.onArrival: they set it down when they see you and look relieved
situations.because: the first sheaf is owed and they cannot afford it
situations.offer: carry it for them and the church credits you the gift

situations.doing: rattling although nothing has been put in
situations.onArrival: the sound stops as you approach
situations.because: the box must be filled and never is
situations.offer: put something in and every locked thing in the church opens once

situations.doing: lighting subscription candles one by one, by name
situations.onArrival: it holds a taper out to you
situations.because: every subscriber must be remembered
situations.offer: light one and it will name who else is still owed

situations.doing: carrying a strongbox toward the altar and back again
situations.onArrival: it asks you to take one end
situations.because: the box must be under the altar and will not fit
situations.offer: help it and it will show you what is beneath

temptations.cue: a chalice used for counting
temptations.benefit: once, ask for a payment and have it given
temptations.standingDrawback: the church books it against you

temptations.cue: one of three keys to the poor box
temptations.benefit: one locked thing per scene opens
temptations.standingDrawback: two other keyholders are missed and looked for

temptations.cue: a sheaf never threshed
temptations.benefit: once, clear a debt owed by anyone
temptations.standingDrawback: the debt transfers rather than clearing

temptations.cue: a tally of every sheaf given
temptations.benefit: once, prove someone owes you
temptations.standingDrawback: your own arrears are on the reverse

temptations.cue: a candle with somebody's name on it
temptations.benefit: light it and that person's ghost assists you, once
temptations.standingDrawback: they expect the favour returned

sanctity.dangerLine: the church minds very much what is brought in, and it can tell

institution: a boot-scraper worn to nothing at the porch
a rail marking where the unbaptised may stand
holy ground marked out by stones set on edge
ritual: a threshold washed daily by nothing
hats removed and hung before a door nobody uses
a censer swung on a chain in an empty aisle
demand: a doorway that will not admit you as you are
a step that is cold through boots
a chancel that makes you aware of your hands
wound: a floor scrubbed through to the bedding mortar
a wall where something was washed off repeatedly
graves outside the wall, in a row, unmarked
anchor: a register of who was clean and who was not
a stone let into the floor, whiter than the rest

features: a threshold recently washed
mud tracked in and scrubbed at, badly
a censer still warm
a hat left on the wrong side of the door
stones set on edge, one moved
a grave dug just outside the wall

decisions.cue: a threshold that will not admit you as you are
decisions.cost: cleaning up costs a moment; forcing it costs more

resolve.success: you make yourself presentable and the church admits you as a guest
resolve.failure: you cross as you are and the ground objects: +1 Bane and the Congregation cools
resolve.orElse: go in by the vestry door: one Turn, and it is noticed

decisions.cue: a rail marking where the unbaptised may stand
decisions.cost: crossing it is either faith or trespass

resolve.success: you cross with the right words and are treated as of the parish
resolve.failure: you cross without them: the next encounter starts hostile
resolve.orElse: stay behind the rail: safe, and you cannot reach what is beyond

decisions.cue: a register of who was clean and who was not
decisions.cost: your names are not in it yet

resolve.success: you enter yourselves convincingly and the church stops testing you
resolve.failure: you enter yourselves badly and are listed among the unclean: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the register; you are tested at every door

decisions.cue: a wall where something was washed off many times
decisions.cost: reading what is under it is possible and unwelcome

resolve.success: you read enough to know what the parish would not have on its wall
resolve.failure: you expose it entirely and the church wants it gone again: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it; the stain stays a stain

decisions.cue: graves outside the wall in an unmarked row
decisions.cost: bringing one inside would settle an old injustice

resolve.success: you move a stone inside the wall and the barred dead are grateful — they will open a way
resolve.failure: you are caught at it and the ground rejects both of you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave them out; they have been out a long time

decisions.cue: a phial of oil, sealed, in the sacristy
decisions.cost: using it consecrates; wasting it does not

resolve.success: you use it exactly and one place becomes safe for the delve
resolve.failure: you spill it and the church counts the waste: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it sealed; nothing is made safe

situations.doing: scrubbing a threshold that is already clean
situations.onArrival: it does not look up and asks you to wipe your feet
situations.because: the ground must be kept and cannot be
situations.offer: wipe your feet and it will let you anywhere, including down

situations.doing: listening at a slot for a confession that has not come
situations.onArrival: it asks, through the wall, whether you have anything to say
situations.because: it may not leave until someone is absolved
situations.offer: tell it one true bad thing and every door in the church opens

situations.doing: swinging on its chain in an aisle with nobody in it
situations.onArrival: the smoke turns toward you
situations.because: the ground must be censed and the thurifer is gone
situations.offer: take the chain and swing it, and what is unclean here withdraws

situations.doing: digging just outside the wall, in the dark
situations.onArrival: they stop and one gestures at the church, resentfully
situations.because: the ground inside was refused them
situations.offer: dig inside for them and the barred dead will carry you through the crypt

situations.doing: standing a little further in than the marks in the grass
situations.onArrival: the boundary has moved since you looked
situations.because: the holy ground is being extended
situations.offer: set one back and the church treats you as a churchwarden

situations.doing: washing a wall where something keeps coming back
situations.onArrival: she hands you a cloth without turning
situations.because: it must not be seen and will not go
situations.offer: read it aloud before you wash it and she will tell you what it means

temptations.cue: a sealed phial of oil
temptations.benefit: once, make a place holy for a scene
temptations.standingDrawback: what was displaced waits at the edge of it

temptations.cue: the register of clean and unclean
temptations.benefit: once, have your presence accepted anywhere here
temptations.standingDrawback: someone else's name has been struck to make room

temptations.cue: a shard of the porch boot-scraper
temptations.benefit: once, cross a threshold that refuses you
temptations.standingDrawback: you bring in whatever the threshold was keeping out

temptations.cue: the whiter stone from the floor
temptations.benefit: stand on it and nothing unclean may touch you
temptations.standingDrawback: you must not step off it while anything is watching

temptations.cue: a censer on a short chain
temptations.benefit: once, drive something back without harming it
temptations.standingDrawback: it remembers the smell and finds you later
